# Sequence searching {#sec-sequence-searching}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Both historical and state-of-the-art methods are used for speed and
accuracy. Understanding the advantages of different algorithms is essential.
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction based on open-access material: homology vs. similarity,
dynamic programming, heuristics for speed, profiles and HMMs for
sensitivity, and how significance (E-values) is estimated.
:::

## Key concepts

- Homology vs. similarity; why similarity implies homology only above a threshold
- Global (Needleman–Wunsch) vs. local (Smith–Waterman) alignment; dynamic programming; gap penalties (linear, affine)
- Substitution matrices: PAM vs. BLOSUM, how they are derived, log-odds scores
- Heuristic search: FASTA, BLAST (seeds, extension, two-hit), BLAT; speed vs. sensitivity
- Statistical significance: extreme value distribution, E-values, bit scores, multiple testing
- Profiles: PSI-BLAST, position-specific scoring matrices, pseudocounts, profile corruption
- Profile hidden Markov models: HMMER, forward/backward, Viterbi; HMM–HMM comparison (HHsearch/HHblits)
- Modern fast search: MMseqs2, DIAMOND; structure-based search (Foldseek)
- Indexing for exact/short matches: suffix trees/arrays, Burrows–Wheeler transform (see also @sec-genomics)
- Multiple sequence alignment: progressive alignment, consistency (T-Coffee), iterative refinement (MUSCLE, MAFFT, Clustal Omega)
- Motif finding: PSSMs/sequence logos, Gibbs sampling, MEME

## Key papers

::: {.callout-tip}
★ = mandatory in earlier reading lists.
:::

### Reviews — start here

- @pearson2013 — an introduction to similarity searching, homology inference and statistics; the best single starting point.
- @eddy2004 — "What is a hidden Markov model?" (two pages).
- @lambert2003 — review of common sequence alignment methods.

### Pairwise alignment and substitution matrices

- @needleman1970 — global alignment by dynamic programming.
- ★ @smith1981 — local alignment.
- @dayhoff1978 — PAM matrices.
- @henikoff1992 — BLOSUM matrices.

### Heuristic database search

- @pearson1988 — FASTA.
- @altschul1990 — the original BLAST.
- ★ @altschul1997 — gapped BLAST and PSI-BLAST.
- @kent2002 — BLAT, for fast genome-scale alignment.
- @steinegger2017 — MMseqs2, sensitive search at scale.
- @buchfink2021 — DIAMOND, BLAST-level sensitivity at much higher speed.

### Profiles and hidden Markov models

- @krogh1994 — profile HMMs for protein families.
- @park1998 — profile methods find three times as many remote homologues as pairwise methods.
- @soding2005 — HMM–HMM comparison (HHsearch).
- @eddy2008 — a probabilistic model of local alignment and significance estimation.
- ★ @eddy2011 — HMMER3: accelerated profile HMM searches.
- ★ @remmert2012 — HHblits.
- @vankempen2024 — Foldseek: searching with structure (3Di alphabet).

### Multiple sequence alignment

- @notredame2000 — T-Coffee (consistency).
- @edgar2004 — MUSCLE.
- @sievers2011 — Clustal Omega.
- @katoh2013 — MAFFT.

### Motif finding

- @lawrence1993 — Gibbs sampling for subtle motifs.
- @bailey1994 — MEME (expectation maximisation).
- @stormo2000 — representation and discovery of DNA binding sites.
